title: Latency‑First Buyer Profiles & Fallback Economics Probe
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a repeatable deliverable that maps enterprise buyer latency tolerance to likely model fallback strategies and the economic impact of each fallback. The deliverable (Competitive Readiness Index, CRI) will inform product rollout priorities for latency-sensitive verticals and provide concrete cost/latency tradeoffs for Sales/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: CRI prototype with scoring for at least 6 enterprise buyer archetypes
Quantified fallback cost delta and expected P99 latency change for top 4 model variants (baseline -> fallback)
Stakeholder review completed (GTM, Solutions, Runtime Eng) and incorporation of feedback
Public deliverable: one-pager + spreadsheet + slide deck for field teams
comments: 2026-02-16 - Asha: Kickoff with Solutions Eng and Sales; collected 7 buyer interviews (annotated). Initial hypothesis: finance/legal buyers trade latency for reproducibility differently vs. customer support teams.

2026-02-22 - Diego: Pulled latency telemetry from console dashboards for top 12 tenant workloads (ENG-20145 provided tokenized traces). Noted bimodal P99 distribution across embeddings vs. chat endpoints.
2026-03-01 - PM review: proposed CRI formula draft: CRI = 0.4*LatencySensitivity + 0.3*ProcurementFriction + 0.2*FallbackQualityRisk + 0.1*RegionalAvailability. Need numeric mapping rationale.
2026-03-05 - Eng feedback (S. Kim): caution: fallback quality risk should include quantization compatibility; add kernel mismatch as a separate multiplier.

2026-03-10 - Diego: ran 3 pilot experiments comparing model A (optimized kernels) -> model B (quantized fallback) on us-west; recorded token cost delta and P99 increase. Uploaded raw CSV to Drive link.
2026-03-12 - Asha: incorporated experiment results and updated spreadsheet; scheduling stakeholder review on 2026-03-18.
Notes: Links to artifacts below include the confluence PRD draft, spreadsheet with telemetry, and a draft field one-pager.
decisions: Decision 2026-03-05: Use a weighted CRI with explicit kernel/quantization penalty as advised by runtime engineering.
Decision 2026-03-11: Limit initial archetypes to 6 (Support, Search, Financial-Desk, Enterprise-Search, Legal-Review, SMB-Chat) to keep pilot manageable.
Decision 2026-03-12: Publish internal CRI and one-pager for Sales; field playbook to be iterative — no external customer-facing collateral in this cycle.
next_steps: Run additional fallback experiments in eu-west region (ENG-20780) to capture regional variance (owner: Diego, due 2026-03-25)
Finalize numeric mappings for procurement friction from interview transcripts (owner: Asha, due 2026-03-18)
Prepare slide deck for 2026-03-18 stakeholder review and incorporate feedback into the final deliverable (owner: Asha)
Add CRI as an input to the model-prioritization playbook (follow-up PM ticket after approval)
notes_for_engineering: Provide kernel-level failure modes and approximate cold-start penalties for each model variant we test.
Label telemetry exports with model_variant and fallback_reason where possible to improve future attribution.
final_deliverables: Stakeholder slide deck with recommended model rollouts and requested runtime mitigations
